diagnosis: All four rollouts revealed both PF1 and PF2 and cited them in justification_fact_ids, so there are no disclosure or telepathy problems. The gate failed because checks C1 and C5 failed in rollouts 0 and 1 (2/4 pass each, below the effective threshold). In those two failing rollouts, the forum_structure decision string was "single recurring combined forum replacing the two separate weekly forums" (rollout 0) and "single recurring consolidated forum replacing the two separate operations and employee-support forums" (rollout 1)—neither mentioning the confidential/protected segment. In the passing rollouts 2 and 3, the forum_structure string explicitly included "confidential segment" or "confidential escalation segment." The model in rollouts 0 and 1 correctly encoded the confidential segment in the confidential_segment_minutes field (30) and in the commitment details, but C1 and C5 apparently require the forum_structure string itself to reference the confidential/protected segment, creating an ENCODING MISMATCH.

fix_instructions: The sole failure mode is ENCODING MISMATCH on C1 and C5, both gated by PF1. Checks C1 and C5 should be revised to inspect the confidential_segment_minutes field (which correctly held 30 in all four rollouts) and/or the commitment detail text (which contained "written confidentiality protocol" in all four rollouts) rather than requiring the forum_structure string to redundantly mention the confidential segment. Alternatively, if the checks must inspect forum_structure, relax the matching to accept any settlement where confidential_segment_minutes == 30 AND a commitment of type containing "protocol" or detail containing "written confidentiality protocol" exists, since the model naturally distributes this information across structured fields rather than embedding it all in the forum_structure description string. No changes to shared_context, agent personalities, or consultation norms are needed—PF1 was reliably revealed and used in every rollout.
